$comment: Cross-rail conformance table for hook-group matcher semantics.
Three runners evaluate the SAME settings.json `matcher` string: the sidecar
and the CLI (cli/src/hooks/run-hooks.ts). They drifted into three different
rules, so the same config behaved differently depending on which shell ran the
turn. The sidecar's rule is canonical because it is the rail that carries the
built-in agent and is what users' existing Claude Code settings were written
against; the other two were aligned to it.
Every runner's test suite reads THIS file, so a future divergence fails a test
on the rail that drifted instead of silently changing behaviour.
3. otherwise                              -> unanchored regex; invalid regex -> no match
`narrow` cases use the tightened exact-set pattern /^[A-Za-z0-9_|]+$/ (split on
| only) that the sidecar applies to FileChanged and StopFailure, whose targets
are file paths and error strings whose punctuation must stay regex-significant.

cases.why: a bare alphanumeric matcher is an EXACT match, not a substring regex
comma is an alternative separator too
alternatives are trimmed, so a spaced list works
underscores stay in the exact-set alphabet
hyphens stay in the exact-set alphabet
punctuation escapes the exact-set path; regex is UNANCHORED at the tail
unanchored head, so a tail anchor matches a suffix
an invalid regex matches nothing rather than throwing

narrowCases.why: pipe set still exact under the narrow alphabet
a path matcher must stay a regex
slashes and dots leave the exact-set path and regex-match themselves
comma is NOT an alternative separator here — it is regex-literal, so the whole string must appear
